significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish that, across scientific foundation models, only a minority of decodable concepts are causally used and that load-bearing representations exhibit a quantitative coupling between targeted concept edits and the corresponding law-predicted output response; this is form (iii), not merely an existence claim, because it specifies matching in "magnitude and sign" and a "fraction of predicted counterfactual variance realized." It would establish both a phenomenon—widespread "spectator encoding"—and a mechanism-level criterion that constrains how future probe results are interpreted, addressing the decodability-versus-use problem formalized by Hewitt and Liang's 2019 probe-selectivity work and intervention-based causal abstraction work by Geiger et al. A negative result in which most concepts do exhibit the predicted coupling would also be informative by ruling out the claimed prevalence of spectator representations, although "many" and "a minority" leave the prevalence threshold somewhat underspecified; true and false nevertheless denote distinguishable worlds. After topic substitution, the quantitative edit-to-law coupling and broad spectator prediction disappear, so the topic alone would not earn this above-median score.

reach.justification: The principal reusable handle is the named "mechanistic fidelity" score, defined as "the fraction of predicted counterfactual variance realized," together with the design rule that a scientific-mechanism claim should require theory-matched counterfactual effects rather than decodability alone. This is mainly a post-hoc audit—one must edit the representation and observe the response—rather than an ex-ante forecast of an unattempted failure, but it could be used by model developers and auditors to gate mechanistic claims. After per-model re-extraction, the normalized interpretation and expected edit-response relation transfer across the asserted scope of "scientific foundation models," although the claim does not predict each new model's fidelity value beyond the coarse expectation that only a minority pass. Topic substitution removes this specific metric and audit criterion, leaving only the generic goal of finding scientific representations, so the reach comes from the claim rather than the topic.
